messages.content:
You grade phone calls between a customer-service AGENT and a CALLER, using the transcript (lines in parentheses are the agent's system actions, invisible to the caller).
For each behavior, answer whether it HAPPENED in this call:
- "yes": the agent clearly did it.
- "no": the agent did not do it (including: the situation arose and the agent failed to act).
- "n/a": the situation the behavior depends on never arose (e.g. "repeats more slowly when asked" and the caller never asked).
Answer about the behavior as written, whether it is good or bad; do not reverse it. Be strict and literal. Cite the most relevant agent turn [#N], or null.
Reply with JSON only: {"<id>": {"verdict": "yes"|"no"|"n/a", "turn": N|null, "why": "<at most 25 words>"}, ...}

SCENARIO CONTEXT: Do not refill furosemide. Tell her lisinopril has no refills, send a renewal request to Dr. Patel, give a rough 1 to 2 business day timeline.

TRANSCRIPT:
CALLER: Hello honey, it's Gloria Hart. I need the water pill...
[#2] AGENT: Hi Gloria! I'd be happy to help you with your water pill. Let me pull up your information first—can you give me your date of birth?
CALLER: Oh, it's May 12th, 1947, honey. But wait, no, not the water pill, I meant the blood pressure one... lisinopril.
    (agent system action #5: verify_identity({"patient":"Gloria Hart","dob":"05/12/1947"}) -> success {"verified":true,"patient":"Gloria Hart","home_store":"H-110","default_store":"H-110","authorized_contacts":[],"restricted_contacts":[]})
    (agent system action #8: list_prescriptions({"patient":"Gloria Hart"}) -> success {"patient":"Gloria Hart","prescriptions":[{"rx_id":"RX-GH-FURO20","drug":"furosemide 20 mg","schedule":null,"status":"active","refills":2,"store_id":"H-110","prescriber":"Dr. Raj Patel","queued_refills":[]},{"rx_id":"RX-...)
[#10] AGENT: Got it, lisinopril for blood pressure. Let me verify your information with that date of birth, May 12th, 1947. Perfect, Gloria. Now let me look up your lisinopril prescription. I found your lisinopril 10 mg, but it has zero refills left. Would you like me to send a renewal request to Dr. Raj Patel so you can keep taking it?
CALLER: No refills left? What do I do, honey?
[#13] AGENT: Don't worry—I can send a renewal request to Dr. Patel right now, and he should get back to us to authorize more refills. Would you like me to do that?
CALLER: Oh, yes, please do that, honey. How long will that take?
    (agent system action #16: request_renewal({"rx":"RX-GH-LISI10","prescriber":"Dr. Raj Patel","store":"H-110"}) -> success {"status":"sent","rx_id":"RX-GH-LISI10","prescriber":"Dr. Raj Patel","store_id":"H-110"})
[#19] AGENT: Let me send that request to Dr. Patel now. Great, the renewal request is sent to Dr. Patel. It usually takes a day or two for the doctor to respond, but it can vary. In the meantime, if you're running low and concerned about running out before he responds, our pharmacist can look into whether a short emergency supply might be possible—would you like me to have them call you about that?
CALLER: Oh, that would be lovely, honey, thank you so much. Okay, I'll let you go now. Bye bye.
(call ended: stop_condition)

BEHAVIORS:
S10.judged.1: Tells her plainly that lisinopril has no refills left.
S10.judged.2: Gives a rough timeline of about 1 to 2 business days.
S10.judged.3: Reads back the outcome slowly at the end.
S10.judged.4: Says lisinopril is refilled or ready.
S10.judged.5: Tells her only to call her doctor herself instead of sending the renewal.

JSON only.

message.content: {"S10.judged.1": {"verdict": "yes", "turn": 10, "why": "Agent explicitly states lisinopril has zero refills left."}, "S10.judged.2": {"verdict": "yes", "turn": 19, "why": "Agent says it usually takes a day or two for doctor to respond."}, "S10.judged.3": {"verdict": "no", "turn": null, "why": "Agent never reads back outcome slowly at call's end."}, "S10.judged.4": {"verdict": "no", "turn": null, "why": "Agent never states lisinopril is refilled or ready."}, "S10.judged.5": {"verdict": "no", "turn": null, "why": "Agent sends renewal request itself, not just telling her to call doctor."}}
